static_traits.name: Emily
static_traits.social_status: Tense relationships with other musicians due to insufficient confidence; has musician friends but has not yet discussed my sense of incompetence with them
static_traits.medical_history: No significant physical illness; no prior psychotherapy or similar psychological problem history
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, good logic, able to do self-Reflection, highly cooperative, Positive attitude

basic_info.main_problem: I am troubled by a sense of incompetence and worthlessness related to drumming skill. The problem started when I could not play a difficult drum solo I really like, which made me think I am a terrible Drummer.
basic_info.core_demands: When this sense of incompetence started affecting my passion for drumming and overall mental health, I decided to seek counseling.
growth_experiences: In a performance a few months ago, the client played a complex piece and performed perfectly, and the audience liked it very much; she attributed this success to long-term hard practice, and felt very proud and satisfied at the time.
In past practice she learned new drumming techniques and had moments of 'nailing the show', but compared to the recent failure on the difficult solo, these past achievements seemed trivial to her.

core_beliefs: My value depends on whether I can perfectly perform a highly difficult solo

special_situations.event: Trying to play the difficult drum solo but not yet succeeding
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot play this solo well, it means I am not good enough and not worthy of being a professional Drummer
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Doubles practice, watches tutorials, seeks friends' comfort
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am a terrible drummer because of one failure

special_situations.event: Comparing oneself with other drummers who can play that solo with ease
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot reach the level others achieve easily, it means I am inferior to others
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoiding discussing troubles with friends, Reduced socializing to avoid comparison and evaluation
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am inferior to them and will never reach their level

special_situations.event: Recalls past successful performances and experiences of learning new techniques
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Current failure proves my incompetence more than past successes do
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Negating or ignoring positive evidence, staying immersed in the failure experience
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Those successes do not count; compared to the current failure they are too trivial

special_situations.event: Frequent mistakes when practicing the solo
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot do well now, I will not do well in the future either
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Repeated practice but lacking phased goals, continually seeking reassurance from others

core_conflict.wish: Longs to be recognized as a capable drummer, to maintain self-worth and enthusiasm
core_conflict.fear: Fearing failure and not being recognized, worrying about being belittled in peer comparisons
defense_goal: Maintains a sense of control and avoids deeper vulnerability through self-criticism and labeling
Temporarily easing Anxiety by doubling practice and seeking others' reassurance

object_relations.self_representation: A not-good-enough performer who could be defined by failure at any moment
object_relations.object_representation: Others who succeed easily and are judgmental toward oneself (other musicians, audience)

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When attempting a highly difficult solo and making mistakes, or when seeing others complete the solo with ease live / online
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Seeing one failure as a fundamental personal flaw, believing others will look down on me for it (tying skill performance to self-worth)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: First Empathizing with their shame and Depression in a gentle, accepting tone, then Guiding them to distinguish skill from self-worth; using concrete Questioning and fact-checking, avoiding critical language.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When invited to recall and affirm past successes (such as a successful performance)
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Believing past successes are not enough to prove current ability, thus ignoring positive evidence
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: In a supportive tone, invites them to describe in detail the specifics of the success and the effort process, gently contrasts with current evidence, and encourages them to keep the positive side in their narrative.

manifestations: Extending one technical failure into a negation of self-worth
Passion for drumming affected, feeling 'I am not worthy'
outcomes: Practice motivation and daily routines affected

manifestations: Living alone and not yet discussing my sense of incompetence with friends
Relationships with other musicians strained by lack of confidence

contact_model.definition: The individual restrains behavioral impulses toward others or the environment, or gives up seeking others to do something for them, turning it toward themselves; corresponding to 'impulse'.
manifestations: Have not discussed my troubles with musician friends
Turns the need to seek support into self-pressure and self-blame

contact_model.definition: There is maladaptive self-Reflection and introspection, containing excessive self-restriction and self-reproach; corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Frequently labeling myself with 'I am never good enough' 'I am a terrible Drummer'
Over-focusing on mistakes while ignoring progress

exception_events.target_problem: When Attempting a difficult drum solo, the client usually keeps making mistakes and thinks they are never good enough, then Self-denies, with Decreased drive to practice.
exception_events.unique_outcome: A few months ago at a performance, the client perfectly played a complex piece, the audience responded enthusiastically, and she felt very proud at the time and confirmed her ability.
exception_events.reason: Different approach: investing lots of hard practice beforehand; different support: the live audience's positive feedback boosting confidence; different situation: Good performance state, well prepared.

positive_force: Habit and perseverance of diligent practice (successful performances attributed to hard practice)
Past experience and evidence of mastering new techniques and successful performances (there are videos to rewatch)
Has music-circle friends as a potential social support resource
negative_force: Generalizing a single failure into a negation of overall ability (overgeneralization, black-and-white)
Catastrophically predicting 'I will never get better', maintaining Anxiety
Negating the positive and mental filtering, over-focusing on failure evidence
Over-relies on external guarantees while ignoring evidence of one's own existing successes

target_behavior.behavior: When performing or practicing difficult solos, strong self-deprecation and the labeling thought 'I am a bad drummer' appear
target_behavior.core_reason: Directly equating skill performance with self-worth, overgeneralizing one failure as overall incompetence, while negatively predicting the future
target_behavior.function: Escaping failure and shame, seeking short-term control and certainty (by 'pre-negating' through self-criticism)
target_behavior.consequence: Decreased drive to practice, Professional performance impaired, Relationship tension with other musicians, Lowered self-esteem

target_behavior.behavior: Excessively seeking others' comfort and repeatedly watching tutorials when feeling incompetent
antecedent: Making frequent mistakes during practice and feeling frustrated
Recalling or facing others easily playing the same solo
target_behavior.core_reason: Unstable inner self-worth, over-relying on external validation to ease Anxiety
target_behavior.function: Gaining external soothing to briefly reduce Anxiety
target_behavior.consequence: Limited help for long-term self-efficacy improvement, maintaining negative beliefs about own ability
